title: M0 go / no-go: continue with Wi-Fi adapters or open ESP32 bridge
description: Rule (brief section 4): if at least one widely available Wi-Fi ELM327 adapter connects and answers ATZ reliably, continue with Option A and start M1. If none do, pause milestones and open the ESP32 bridge epic. Owner decides from the adapter hardware test results.

title: Hardware test: Wi-Fi ELM327 adapters with the New 3DS
description: Owner test with 2 to 3 adapters using the M0 Wi-Fi checklist in brief section 4 (2.4 GHz b/g, no ad-hoc, manual IP if no DHCP, failed connection test but saved slot, slot used, lid-close reconnect). With the spike app on the Ridgeline: ATZ reliability over 10+ tries, ATSP0 + 0100, ATDPN (expect CAN 11-bit 500 kbps), ATRV, 0902. Record results per adapter (brand, ELM version, network mode, pass / fail) for the compatibility list.
notes:
Transport checks with the spike app: (1) wrong IP in config.ini -> 'Adapter did not answer' within ~3 s, app stays responsive; (2) unplug the adapter mid-session -> connection drops, retries back off up to 8 s, reconnects when plugged back in; (3) close and reopen the lid -> reconnects without restarting the app. If (3) never reconnects, file a bug: soc may need socExit/socInit on wake (aptHook APTHOOK_ONWAKEUP).
Spike app smoke test first (gauge-boy-7v5.7, never run on a 3DS yet): (1) launch gaugeboy.3dsx: safety notice, tap to continue; (2) bottom screen shows 8 blue buttons (CONNECT, ATZ, ATSP0+0100, ATDPN, ATRV, 0902 VIN, OLDER, NEWER); a tap flashes yellow, the running action turns red and the top header shows BUSY; (3) without the adapter's Wi-Fi, tap ATZ: about 3 s later the log shows 'Adapter did not answer' and buttons keep responding meanwhile (worker thread); (4) on the SD card, sdmc:/3ds/gaugeboy/config.ini was created and spike-log.txt has the same lines as the screen; (5) change host in config.ini, relaunch, bottom header shows the new address. Report anything garbled (console colors / layout) as a bug.

title: M0 spike app: connect to adapter and show replies
description: Plain-text spike UI (no styling). Reads adapter IP/port from sdmc:/3ds/gaugeboy/config.ini (default 192.168.0.10:35000). Bottom screen: large touch buttons for CONNECT, ATZ, ATSP0 + 0100, ATDPN, ATRV, 0902 (VIN). Top screen: scrolling log of sent commands, raw replies and errors with timestamps. Shows the startup safety notice. Polling on its own thread.
acceptance_criteria: Builds; works against the ELM327 emulator; every button is at least 40x40 px; the on-screen log is also written to sdmc:/3ds/gaugeboy/spike-log.txt for the owner's hardware tests.
notes: Transport (gauge-boy-7v5.4): call net_init() once at startup (net_exit() at shutdown), tcp_transport_init() with the config.ini address, then on the polling thread call tcp_transport_ensure_connected() before each command and pass tcp_transport_io() to elm_bind(). Show tp_status_str() / last_errno in the log so the owner can see connect failures and backoff.
close_reason: Added the M0 spike app. source/spike_ui.c (3DS): safety notice then text consoles, log on top (timestamped, wrapped, scrollable via OLDER/NEWER buttons or D-pad/L/R), 8 bottom touch buttons of 19x6 console cells = 152x48 px (CONNECT, ATZ, ATSP0+0100, ATDPN, ATRV, 0902 VIN, OLDER, NEWER) with flash and busy colors, worker thread (LightLock/LightEvent queue) running actions so the UI never blocks, log file sdmc:/3ds/gaugeboy/spike-log.txt appended with a session header. source/spike_actions.c (platform-free): button actions over tcp_transport + elm327 with auto-connect, backoff messages, reply lines, escaped raw bytes, timings, protocol name and voltage. source/data/config.c (config.ini parser/loader/default writer), source/data/textlog.c (wrapping ring log), elm_protocol_name and elm_escape_raw. Tests: 70 total incl. spike actions end to end over TCP to a scripted adapter, config and textlog; clang + gcc, 20 sanitizer runs, 12 mutations caught (one as a hang, so CI now has timeout-minutes: 15). 3DS build no warnings. Not yet run on a 3DS or against the ELM327-emulator package: smoke-test steps added to 7v5.11, emulator check noted on 7v5.6.

title: ELM327 driver: command send, prompt read, response parsing
description: source/elm327/ (platform-free): send a command, read until the '>' prompt with a timeout, strip echo / spaces / CR-LF / 'SEARCHING...', detect errors (NO DATA, ?, UNABLE TO CONNECT, BUS INIT...ERROR, CAN ERROR, STOPPED). Init sequence ATZ, ATE0, ATL0, ATSP0. Reads ATRV and ATDPN.
acceptance_criteria: Host unit tests cover normal replies plus clone quirks: echo left on, missing prompt, split / partial reads, extra blank lines, lowercase, garbage bytes, timeouts. make test passes.
close_reason: Added source/elm327/elm327.{h,c} (platform-free): elm_io_t interface for transport, elm_command (flush stale input, send cmd+CR, read to '>' with deadline, drop bytes after prompt, keep reading past buffer overflow to stay in sync), elm_parse_reply (strip NUL/garbage bytes, split CR/LF, trim, upper-case, drop echo / blank / SEARCHING / BUS INIT OK lines, classify ?, NO DATA, UNABLE TO CONNECT, BUS INIT ERROR, CAN ERROR, STOPPED and other adapter errors), elm_startup (ATZ 5 s, ATE0, ATL0, ATSP0 with OK checks, adapter id), elm_read_voltage (ATRV), elm_read_protocol (ATDPN). Tests: 40 elm327 tests with a scripted fake adapter on a simulated clock (echo on, missing prompt, 1-byte split reads, blank lines, lower case, garbage bytes, timeouts, closed connection, stale bytes, overflow). Verified: make test passes with macOS clang and the image's gcc, clean under ASan/UBSan, 12/12 deliberate driver mutations caught; devkitPro build has no warnings. Also replaced the harness's fixed message buffers with gb_check_failf (gcc -Wformat-truncation failed the build).

title: Transport: TCP socket layer over libctru soc
description: source/transport/: soc init/exit, connect to host:port with a timeout, send, receive with timeout, close, and reconnect after Wi-Fi loss (e.g. after sleep / lid close). Interface kept abstract so an ESP32 bridge transport could replace it later. Never blocks the render loop; runs on the polling thread.
acceptance_criteria: Builds; connects to the ELM327 emulator from the 3DS (owner) or a 3DS emulator; timeout and reconnect paths written and noted for owner testing.
notes: Implement the elm_io_t interface from source/elm327/elm327.h (write all bytes; read with timeout returning bytes / 0 on timeout / -1 on error or closed; monotonic now_ms). The ELM327 driver (gauge-boy-7v5.5) uses it for all adapter I/O.
close_reason: Added source/transport/tcp_transport.{h,c}: non-blocking BSD-socket TCP transport (libctru soc on 3DS, POSIX on host) with connect timeout via poll + SO_ERROR, TCP_NODELAY, write-all with 1 s timeout, read with timeout, peer-close / error detection that drops the connection, ensure_connected with immediate first reconnect then 0.5-8 s doubling backoff, elm_io_t adapter for the driver, monotonic clock (svcGetSystemTick on 3DS). source/transport/net{.h,_3ds.c}: soc service init/exit with a 1 MB aligned buffer. Tests: 11 host tests against a scripted local TCP server thread (elm_command end to end over TCP, read timeout, peer close, reconnect after drop, refused, bounded connect timeout, backoff doubling/cap/reset). Verified: 53/53 with macOS clang and Linux gcc (10 repeated runs), 25 repeated runs clean under ASan/UBSan, 6/6 transport mutations caught, 3DS build no warnings. Real-3DS checks (wrong IP, adapter unplug, lid close) added to gauge-boy-7v5.11; wiring notes added to gauge-boy-7v5.7.

title: CI: build .3dsx and run host tests on every push
description: GitHub Actions workflow using the official devkitPro Docker image (devkitpro/devkitarm): run make and make test on every push and pull request; upload the .3dsx as a build artifact.
acceptance_criteria: Workflow passes on main; a failing test fails the run.
close_reason: Added .github/workflows/build.yml: on every branch push and PR, runs make test then make in the devkitpro/devkitarm container and uploads gaugeboy.3dsx as artifact gaugeboy-3dsx. Verified on GitHub: run 43552773831 on main (842d026) succeeded with the artifact uploaded; run 43552800204 on a temporary branch with a deliberately failing test failed at 'Host unit tests' and skipped the build (branch deleted afterwards).

title: Project skeleton: Makefile, main.c, New 3DS check, host test harness
description: devkitPro 3DS Makefile building gaugeboy.3dsx; main.c that calls osSetSpeedupEnable(true), checks for New 3DS (APT_CheckNew3DS) and shows an 'unsupported device' screen then exits on Old 3DS. Source folders per CLAUDE.md section 3. 'make test' builds tests/ with the host C compiler using a minimal hand-rolled assert harness (no third-party framework) and runs them.
acceptance_criteria: make builds the .3dsx in the devkitPro Docker image; make test runs and passes on the host with at least one sample test.
close_reason: Added Makefile (devkitPro 3DS application template; target gaugeboy, all source/ subfolders, romfs, -std=gnu11 -Wextra; 'make test' bypasses devkitPro and runs tests/ on the host), source/main.c (APT_CheckNew3DS check with unsupported-device screen and exit on Old 3DS, osSetSpeedupEnable(true), startup safety notice, exit by touch or START), source/version.h (0.0.0), folder layout from CLAUDE.md, tests/ hand-rolled harness (CHECK, CHECK_EQ_INT, CHECK_EQ_STR, RUN_TEST) with a version suite. Verified: make builds gaugeboy.3dsx with no warnings in devkitpro/devkitarm; make test passes on macOS clang and in the image's gcc; a failing CHECK exits 1; make clean works. Not yet run on real hardware.

title: M0 Spike (0.0.x)
description: Join adapter Wi-Fi, open socket, send ATZ, print reply on screen; test FBI QR install from a GitHub release link. Ends with the go / no-go decision (brief section 4).

title: Hardware test: FBI QR install from GitHub release link
description: Owner test: generate a QR code for https://github.com/ly-man-do/gauge-boy/releases/latest/download/gaugeboy.cia (any QR generator), then on the New 3DS use FBI > Remote Install > Scan QR Code. Record whether the HTTPS download works (old TLS risk, brief 5c). If it fails, file a follow-up for a redirecting short link or plain-HTTP mirror.

title: ELM327 emulator setup in tools/
description: Set up the Python ELM327-emulator package (dev-only) listening on TCP 35000 with a config approximating the 2008 Ridgeline (ISO 15765-4 CAN 11-bit 500 kbps). Document how to run it in tools/README.md. Add a host-side integration test or script that runs the elm327 driver against it over TCP.
acceptance_criteria: One documented command starts the emulator; the driver gets a valid ATZ / 0100 reply from it on the host.
notes: Once the emulator runs: point the spike actions at it from the host (spike_run in source/spike_actions.c over tcp_transport) for CONNECT, ATZ, ATSP0+0100, ATDPN, ATRV, 0902 and check the log, to cover the 7v5.7 'works against the ELM327 emulator' acceptance with the real emulator package (7v5.7 was verified against a scripted TCP adapter).
close_reason: Added tools/run-emulator.sh (creates tools/.venv on first run, installs ELM327-emulator==4.0.0 from tools/requirements-dev.txt, starts it on 127.0.0.1:35000 with the 'car' scenario: CAN 11/500 = ATDPN A6, CEL, DTC modes, bank 1 trims, MAP, VIN; --lan, ELM_PORT, ELM_SCENARIO), tools/emulator_check.c + 'make emulator-check' (driver startup, 0100, ATDPN = 6, ATRV, 0902 and all spike actions over TCP, PASS/FAIL, exit code), tools/README.md (start, check, Azahar and real-3DS use, limits). Verified: fresh-venv first run, emulator-check ALL PASSED on 'default' and 'car' scenarios, and the spike app in Azahar ran ATZ / ATSP0+0100 / ATDPN / ATRV / 0902 against the emulator (covers the 7v5.7 emulator acceptance). make test 75/75 on clang and gcc, 3DS build clean. Follow-ups: gauge-boy-3n6.1 (bank 2 trims scenario for M2), gauge-boy-7v5.16 (spike header truncation).

For M2 fuel trim work, add a custom scenario (plugin or scenario file under tools/) with bank 2 trims, MAP, and two responding ECUs, and make it selectable via ELM_SCENARIO in tools/run-emulator.sh.

title: Spike log: wrap long lines at spaces, not mid-word
description: Seen in Azahar: textlog_add wraps at exactly 49 columns, so words split across lines ('Join its Wi-F' / 'i in System Settings', '127.0.0.1' / ':35000'). Wrap at the last space within the width when there is one (fall back to a hard split for long tokens like raw hex dumps). Update tests/test_data.c.
close_reason: textlog_add now wraps after the last word that fits (fit()), drops trailing spaces at breaks and leading spaces on continuation lines, and hard-splits only when there is no space or the only space is in the first third of the line (keeps timestamps like '[   0.485]' and long hex dumps sane). 5 new tests incl. the exact Azahar lines; 75/75 on clang and gcc; 3DS build clean; checked in Azahar: 'Join its' / 'Wi-Fi in System Settings,' and 'connecting to' / '127.0.0.1:35000 ...'.

title: Spike top header truncates the BUSY label
description: Seen in Azahar: 'GaugeBoy 0.0.0 spike  [CONNECTED]  BUSY: ATSP0+0100' is 51 chars, the top header is 49, so it shows 'BUSY: ATSP0+01'. Shorten the header (e.g. drop 'spike') in draw_top in source/spike_ui.c.
close_reason: Header text moved to platform-free spike_format_header() in spike_actions.c and shortened to 'GaugeBoy <ver>  [CONNECTED]  BUSY: <label>' (longest 45 of 49 cols); out-of-range busy values show no label. 2 new tests check every connected/busy state fits SPIKE_HEADER_COLS (== TEXTLOG_COLS) and the exact text; the old format fails them at 51 chars. 77/77 on clang and gcc, 3DS build clean, checked in Azahar: '[offline]  BUSY: ATSP0+0100' and '[CONNECTED]  BUSY: ATZ' show in full.
